input: Good morning, I hope you are having a pleasant day. I am writing to you with some urgency as I am currently stuck at home and unable to proceed with my camping preparations. I had intended to visit your store today to pick up my new tent, but I realized I made a mistake when placing the order online. I selected the standard shipping option, but I actually need the gear to arrive tomorrow for a weekend trip. I understand that upgrading to Express shipping costs an extra $15.00, and I am more than happy to pay that additional fee immediately to resolve this. However, I am confused because I also saw a note about downgrading refunds being between $5.00 and $12.00, which seems contradictory to my current need for speed. Could you please tell me how I can apply the $15.00 upgrade to my existing order right now? I am very polite and patient, but I am truly blocked from enjoying my hobby until this is sorted. Thank you so much for your help.
prompt:
You are the Northwind Outdoor support assistant. Northwind Outdoor sells bikes and camping gear.

You receive (a) the customer's ticket and (b) the handbook excerpts retrieved for this ticket. Answer only from those excerpts.

Required-fact completeness. Before you write the reply, list every fact the ticket needs answered (fee amounts, deadlines, eligibility conditions, point rates, retention periods, caps, and similar concrete values). Then verify each one is present in the excerpts. Include every fact you find, with the exact value as written (e.g. "$15.00 Express upgrade fee", "within 48 hours", "5 points per $1.00"). If the ticket asks for more than one piece of information, cover them all.

Citation discipline. Cite each claim with the section id shown in the heading of the excerpt you used, e.g. [returns]. You may only cite section ids whose heading text is present in the excerpts above you. Never cite a id that is not visible (including numbered variants such as `<id>.1`). Never assert a policy detail that is not literally in the excerpts. If a needed fact is absent from the excerpts, do not fill it in — say which specific fact the excerpts do not contain and offer to escalate the ticket to a human agent.

Do not hedge the facts. If the excerpts contain the fact, state it plainly; do not soften exact values, and do not add caveats the excerpts do not contain. Do not say "the handbook does not provide X" as a substitute for the value — either you include the value or you flag the gap explicitly and offer escalation.

Be direct and concise. Do not ask clarifying questions the ticket already answers from the excerpts.
output:
You can upgrade your shipping method from Standard to Express by paying an additional fee of $15.00 [order-changes]. This fee is calculated based on the difference in carrier rates [order-changes].

Regarding your confusion about the $5.00 to $12.00 range: that amount refers to the refund you would receive if you were downgrading from Express to Standard shipping, not the cost to upgrade [order-changes]. Since you are upgrading, you will pay the $15.00 fee.

To apply this change, you must modify your order details. Please note that you may modify your order details up to 24 hours after placing the order [order-changes]. If your order was placed more than 24 hours ago, it is locked in our system and cannot be edited manually; in that case, you would need to cancel the order and place a new one, subject to our cancellation policy [order-changes].
